children: Mumbai: S&P Global Ratings on Friday downgraded the credit ratings of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) and its wholly-owned units, stating weaker-than-expected operating performance at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is weighing on total profits and cash flows. The rating agency lowered its long-term issuer credit rating on TMPV and unit TML Holdings to 'BBB-' from 'BBB', while revising the outlook to stable from negative. It cut JLR's rating to 'BB+' from 'BBB-', also with a stable outlook against a negative outlook earlier.
"Weak profitability and negative free operating cash flow (FOCF) at Jaguar Land Rover Automotive PLC will likely delay financial recovery at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles," S&P said.

British luxury carmaker JLR, which contributes about 80% of TMPV's consolidated revenue, is expected to remain a drag on the Indian automaker's earnings. S&P estimates TMPV's adjusted Ebitda margin will improve marginally to about 0.4% in FY27 from 0.2% last year.

The agency expects JLR to face continued pressure from weak sales volume and challenging market conditions. Sales of imported vehicles in China fell 35% year-on-year in the first half of FY27, further clouding the automaker's recovery prospects. S&P has pushed back its expectation of JLR turning free cash flow positive to FY28 from FY27, citing the weaker operating environment.
JLR's financial performance has also been hit by restructuring-related costs and a major product portfolio refresh.

The company reported exceptional items of 530 million in the September quarter, including separation costs and write-downs of intangible assets under development. It has lowered its full-year revenue guidance to 25 billion and expects a pre-tax margin of 2-3%, citing geopolitical risks and restructuring costs.

S&P expects JLR's annual capital expenditure and research and development spending to remain elevated at 3.3-3.4 billion over FY27 and FY28 as it undertakes the portfolio refresh. This is expected to result in adjusted negative FOCF of about 1.4 billion in FY27.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

title: S&P cuts Tata Motors PV ratings on weaker JLR margins, poor cash
